consentNote: It won't give doses, rates or money advice.

profile.title: About your farm
profile.intro: Two taps, so the coach uses examples from your kind of farm.

fac-01-on-your-place.title: AI on your place
fac-01-on-your-place.question: Pick one tool on your farm that might use AI. What does it sense or predict?
fac-01-on-your-place.context: Lesson 2 covered tools that already use AI on NZ farms: collars, drafting, milk meters, weather and pasture apps. Each one senses or predicts. None of them is always right.
lookFor: Says what it senses or predicts
Gives a practical way to notice when it's wrong
fac-01-on-your-place.pushOn: How would you know if it got it wrong?
watchFor: If they bring up animal health or a dose, don't confirm or correct it.
fac-01-on-your-place.example: Our weather app. It predicts rain for the district. I'd know it was wrong by checking the gauge at the woolshed.

fac-01-trust.title: When would you trust it?
fac-01-trust.question: Name one farm job you'd give a chat AI this week, and one question you'd check before you trusted its answer. Why the difference?
fac-01-trust.context: Lesson 3 covered what chat AI is good at (drafting, summing up, explaining, sorting) and where it goes wrong: it can state made-up facts and figures and sound sure, and it knows nothing about your farm unless you tell it.
lookFor: Says what makes one safe and the other not
watchFor: Doses, rates and withholding periods: don't confirm or correct. Money decisions: no advice either way.
fac-01-trust.example: I'd get it to tidy my notes from the stock agent's call, because I know what was said. I wouldn't trust it on this week's lamb schedule. It could give an old price.

fac-01-draft-a-text.title: Get it to draft a text
fac-01-draft-a-text.task: Get the AI to draft a short text to a neighbour, contractor or stock agent about a real job this week.
fac-01-draft-a-text.starterPrompt: I farm near {town}. Shearing is booked for the second week of December. Write a short text to my shearing contractor checking they're still on for that week.
fac-01-draft-a-text.scope: drafting a short everyday text message or email about farm work
fac-01-draft-a-text.offTask: This box only drafts a short message. Try that one in your own AI app, and check what it says.
fac-01-draft-a-text.context: Lesson 4 is a first conversation with a chat AI: ask, read the answer, then follow up to make it better.
lookFor: Says what the job is and when
Asks for a length or a tone

closing.question: Was the second draft better than the first? What did your follow-up change?
closing.example: The first one was too long and too polite. I asked for shorter, and the second was close to what I'd write myself. I changed one word.

fac-01-rain.title: Ask about your rain
fac-01-rain.task: Ask the AI how much rain your district has had since 1 July, and if that's normal.
fac-01-rain.starterPrompt: How much rain has the {town} district had since 1 July, and is that normal?
fac-01-rain.scope: rain since 1 July for one New Zealand district or farm
fac-01-rain.offTask: This box only does rain questions. Try that one in your own AI app, and check what it says.
fac-01-rain.context: Lesson 5: the same question twice. First with no data, then with a rain card of real figures for the farm. The point is what changes.

closing.question: What can't AI know about your farm's rain, even with the rain card?
closing.example: Our back hill catches more rain than the gauge in the valley.

fac-01-tell-a-mate.title: Tell a mate
fac-01-tell-a-mate.question: What's the one thing from today you'd tell a mate about AI? Write it the way you'd say it.
fac-01-tell-a-mate.context: Module 1 covered: what AI is, where it already is on farms, what chat AI is good at and gets wrong, a first conversation, and asking with real data.
fac-01-tell-a-mate.example: Asked AI about our rain with no data and it wasn't much use. Gave it the real figures and it could tell me we're well ahead of normal. Same app, same question.
